To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the concept of the body is not limited to the organic body, but includes the relational body, (ii) the body is not an object but an agent, (iii) the body is a subject, (iv) the body is an entity, (v) the body is in a state of tension, (vi) the body is both subject and object, (vii) the body can be understood as an agent and an entity, (ix) the body is the agent
(1) the concept of the body is a central one in the works of Merleau-Ponry and Lacan

the use of a combination of the following three approaches is the best way to understand the concept of the body : (1) the phenomenological analysis of lived experience, (2) the psychoanalytical theory of the body as a subject of desire and the body of the other as the object of desire, and (3) the topological theory of the body in its relation to the world.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the human body, the body of the other and the body of the world.
the question of how the body can be thought of as both organic and relational.
the relationship between the human and its environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while Merleau-Pon-ty’s philosophy of embodiment is certainly a valuable resource, it is also necessary to introduce a dualistic dimension to account for the death drive.
the Lacanian concept of the Real, as the limit of the symbolic, is the most suitable for describing the nature of the body as a living organism and as a lived body.

the work of Duportail, although not without its limits, is an important contribution to the field of the phenomenology of the body, in particular in the way it brings the Lacanian theory of the subject and the topological model of the body to the fore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subject is always a subject of desire, but that the subject of desire is also always a subject of the death drive.
the body is a complex system of relations, a network, which is not only biological and material, but also symbolic and relational.
the body is not a simple container of desire but that desire is also a way of being in the world and of being with others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of the body as a living entity is not enough to explain how the subject is able to relate to the world and to the other.
the presence of a hole in the tissue of flesh is a necessary condition for a subject to maintain his/her integrity and avoid being absorbed by the world.
